▪︎Sx also when mean transvalvular gradient >40 mm Hg; nl Aov area = 3–4 cm²
▪︎aSx period 1st → most common Sx: DOE/⇣exercise tolerance, exertional dizziness (presyncope) or syncope, + exertional angina
▪︎severe AS: paradoxical S2 split (A usually closes b4 P; in severe AS P closes b4 A; worse w expiration & better w inspiration)
▪︎echo = definitive dx test (leaflets thickened + calcified w/ ⇣systolic motion + sm aortic orifice); Doppler: transaortic velocity + LV-aortic gradient + valve area → severity
•used as a bridge to AVR, if ⍉a surg candidate, or in peds
▪︎⍉surgical candidates / refusing surgery → medical mgmt; symptomatic severe AS w/o AVR → poor prognosis

Almost always congenital & a dz of the young
▪︎PE: JVP a wave prominence, L parasternal lift

rheumatic fever MCC in developing countries
▪︎⇣CO + ⇡LA pressure 2/2 backflow → pulm HTN → exertional dyspnea + fatigue

MVP = MCC of MR in the US
gel like sugar complex build up  -connective tissue dz
Poss narrow AP diameter, ↓body wt, hypotension, scoliosis, pectus excavatum
: posterior bulging leaflets w tissue redundancy
▪︎dx criterion: leaflet displacement ≥2mm above mitral annulus (long axis view)
▪︎palpitations → eval for underlying dysrhythmia; anxiety → eval for anxiety d/o
▪︎MC innocent murmur of childhood; benign, no structural ♡ dz
▪︎up to 85% of children; MC 3–7 y/o; boys = girls; pathophys unknown
▪︎3 types: Still (MC), pulmonic murmurs, venous hums
▪︎concerning features (→ ⍉innocent): chest pain, palpitations, syncope, growth delay, excessive sleepiness, cyanosis
Low-pitched at lower lt sternal area; vibratory, musical quality; no-min radiation to apex (vs AS → often radiates to neck); precordium quiet, S1 nl, ⍉additional ♡ sounds (gallops, clicks, rubs)
▪︎grade ≤2/6; short systolic (⍉holosystolic, ⍉diastolic); softer sitting vs supine (exception: venous hum = louder sitting)
▪︎standing: supine → standing ⇣ both AS + innocent murmur (⇣preload, ⇣ventricular size, ⇣ventricular filling)
▪︎lateral recumbent: ⍉affect Still murmur; squatting: ⇡venous return → ⇡preload → ⇡AS murmur; ⍉affect Still

▪︎pathologic (chart): grade ≥3, holosystolic (VSDs, small muscular defects, regurg), max intensity LUSB (ASD, pulm stenosis), harsh/blowing, abnl S2, systolic click, diastolic murmur, ⇡intensity w/ upright, gallop (S3/S4), friction rub (pericarditis)

▪︎other causes of midsystolic murmurs: ⇡flow across nl semilunar valves (high-output/hyperdynamic states); obstruction (stenosis) of ventricular outflow; ejection into a dilated great vessel beyond the valve
▪︎nl vitals, pulses, O2 sat, CXR, ECG
No tx required; no activity restrictions; no specific f/u or routine testing recommended
